=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/validate_process.sh:4560-4561 (escalation block 5377-5397) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The PRIOR_COMMENTS fetch keeps only the last three comments matching "Runtime validation" (`.[-3:]`), so by cycle 3 the cycle-1 fingerprint marker is outside the window and PRIOR_FINGERPRINT_HITS stays below 2.
  WHY: Cross-cycle escalation from needs_fixes to harness_error never fires in production, and the new test injects both markers directly so it misses this. Severity disagreement: MAJOR (sonnet, luna, glm) vs BLOCKER (minimax); highest used.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:2829-2836 | severity=major | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The resolver picks the newest dispatch comment (`$trusted[-1]`), but post_tracking_comment edits an older same-body comment in place (orchestrate_poll_process.sh:3166-3195), so after a /revalidate reset to cycle 1 the newest comment is still the stale higher-cycle one.
  WHY: A run that is really cycle 1 derives a higher cycle, which gives the wrong fix-up issue name and can trigger escalation against stale markers. Confidence varies (3 to 5).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:15151-15169 (and scripts/validate_process.sh:2824-2857) | severity=blocker | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The poller dispatches the validation workflow before it posts the cycle dispatch comment, so a fast run can read the previous cycle's comment and derive cycle N-1.
  WHY: The run uses a stale cycle for prior context, the fix-up issue name and the escalation gate. Severity disagreement: NIT (sonnet), MAJOR (luna, glm), BLOCKER (minimax); highest used.
- scripts/validate_process.sh:2818-2825 | severity=major | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: validation_cycle_resolve makes its own paginated comments request instead of reusing the PRIOR_COMMENTS snapshot the issue names.
  WHY: It costs one extra API call per run and departs from the issue's wording.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: When VALIDATION_CYCLE is unset or empty, derive it from the newest "Runtime validation dispatched" comment in the tracking comments the script already fetches (PRIOR_COMMENTS), counting only comments by the pipeline login.
  expected_change_site: scripts/validate_process.sh, validation_cycle_resolve and the PRIOR_COMMENTS fetch (4558-4561)
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: validation_cycle_resolve (lines 2818-2825) issues a separate paginated comments request, the PRIOR_COMMENTS request at 4560-4561 is unchanged, and the resolver does not consume that snapshot. Severity: NIT (glm), MAJOR (minimax, luna). Sonnet and qwen judged this justified and did not report it.
- requirement: Tests (tests/test_validate_process_cross_cycle_escalation.py): escalation firing at a derived cycle of 3.
  expected_change_site: tests/test_validate_process_cross_cycle_escalation.py, test_escalation_fires_at_derived_cycle_three
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: The test (line 465) injects PRIOR_COMMENTS directly and never exercises the production fetch at scripts/validate_process.sh:4560-4561, so it passes despite the `.[-3:]` truncation bug.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

  WHY: PRIOR_FINGERPRINT_HITS stays at 1 or less, so needs_fixes is never promoted to harness_error. The new test bypasses the fetch.
